long_biography.plain_text:
Levett developed practical expertise in commercial-vehicle maintenance through a Victoria bodyworks business, which he sold before becoming a transport consultant. He advised Pacific Coach Lines on maintenance and in 1984 was named among the principals forming a private successor company to operate the Vancouver-Victoria route.

Beyond commercial transport, Levett developed a second public identity as a captain and coastal operator. Drawing on more than five decades in British Columbia waters, he led a multiyear preservation effort for an important 1930 wooden maritime craft. He retained historic furnishings and machinery while returning it to charter service. The project linked technical maintenance, hospitality and maritime stewardship.
